answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring every new account to post stake and obtain endorsements from several older, independently trusted accounts before it can trade at scale. A random prism audit asks endorsers to validate the same signed history; if a sybil cluster is exposed, the new account and its endorsers lose stake and opal reputation. The attacker must fund many deposits, recruit real trust, and build a ridge of credibility while risking slashing, so fake identities cost more than they earn.
